strengths: Clear identification of inverted U-shaped correlation between chain length and accuracy with strong empirical motivation
Consistent improvements across both HoVer and EX-FEVER benchmarks (73.42% vs 69% on 2-hop; 75% vs 72.8% on 3-hop), with particularly strong performance on harder scenarios
Comprehensive statistical analysis in appendix demonstrating systematic structural changes (p < 1e-30) and effective decoupling of variable generation from path formation (correlation 0.16 vs 0.85)
Well-structured methodology with clear two-stage training pipeline (SFT + GRPO) and composite reward function targeting identified trade-offs
Solid technical execution with appropriate application of GRPO and rigorous ablation showing GRPO > CPO > SFT
weaknesses: Overclaimed causal grounding: implemented as template-based structured prompting, not true causal inference; lacks interventional queries, counterfactuals, or formal causal identification—SCM framing is misleading about novelty

Data construction quality not validated: consistency filtering only checks final answer correctness, not intermediate causal components (U, V, F); no reported pass rates or analysis of biases; structured prompting strategy underspecified and difficult to reproduce
Critical ablation missing: no SFT+GRPO (no SCM) baseline to isolate whether improvements come from SCM, GRPO algorithm, or composite rewards; no per-component reward ablations (R_c, R_s, R_l)

Reward function design lacks principled justification: Structure reward Δ(y)=|U|-|V| assumes more evidence always better; hyperparameters (γ, δ, λ, β_s, β_l) appear arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis; [l_min, l_max] determination unclear

Limited experimental scope: only 2 benchmarks, max 3-4 hops; acknowledges inability to handle ultra-long chains but provides no empirical verification; no generalization to other MHFV datasets or reasoning tasks

Statistical rigor concerns: Table 1 reports single runs with no error bars or confidence intervals; no disclosed number of seeds/runs; mixed baseline comparisons (GPT-3.5 vs Qwen3-8B); inconsistent backbone choices in 'Pure LLM' section

Reproducibility gaps: hyperparameter values not specified; training details sparse (learning rate, batch size, epochs missing); data construction pipeline insufficiently detailed; no template examples; code unavailability mentioned
Underexplored empirical findings: optimal chain length varies by hop count but no adaptive strategy proposed; no failure case analysis; unclear when method breaks down on genuinely complex reasoning

strengths: Novel empirical insight into the inverted U-shaped relationship between reasoning chain length and accuracy, well-demonstrated across multiple settings
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with solid ablation studies and detailed structural analysis showing statistical significance of improvements
Well-designed data construction pipeline with consistency filtering and reasonable error rates (~1%)
Achieves competitive performance on established benchmarks (HoVer and EX-FEVER) with explicit graph-based traceability (>95% structural faithfulness)
Clear and honest presentation of methodology, appropriately positioning SCM as structural dependency abstraction rather than full causal inference
Thoughtful impact statement acknowledging limitations and appropriate cautionary guidance for deployment
weaknesses: Concerning performance degradation when applying SCM-CoT without GRPO (Qwen3-14B: 57.48% → 47.22% on HoVer 2-hop) suggests the mechanism itself is poorly calibrated; explanation remains descriptive rather than mechanistic
Modest improvements over same-backbone baselines (e.g., 0.86% over Direct Prediction on HoVer 2-hop), making it difficult to assess the true contribution independent of architectural differences
High hyperparameter sensitivity with no principled selection method: accuracy varies from 0.6433 to 0.7544 based on reward weights (Table 4); length range selection relies on training set tuning
Shallow connection between SCM formulation and actual implementation: no deep insights into why DAG structure helps; structural functions F are only used during data construction, not optimization

Reward function design lacks theoretical justification: Structure Reward encourages minimizing intermediate steps via crude heuristics (|U| - |V|), potentially harming problems requiring complex inference
Structural faithfulness metric insufficient: only checks DAG validity, not semantic correctness of inferences; no manual evaluation of reasoning quality
Limited generalization analysis: unverified scalability to chains >4 hops, no out-of-domain evaluation, optimal chain length [80-160 tokens] may be dataset-specific
Incomplete technical details: enforcement of structural validity constraints during inference unclear, GRPO hyperparameters (group size K) not fully specified, no computational cost comparison
Data construction relies on teacher model 4x larger than student (30B vs 8B), with only 60% of training data distilled; no analysis of impact on quality
Comparison with simpler alternatives (length penalties, reranking) dismissed without thorough empirical evaluation despite acknowledged efficiency concerns

strengths: Strong empirical results on HoVer and EX-FEVER benchmarks with consistent improvements over baselines, achieving 71.02% average accuracy while using a smaller Qwen3-8B model compared to GPT-3.5-based competitors
Valuable empirical observation about inverted U-shaped relationship between reasoning chain length and verification accuracy, supported by clear visualization and analysis
Rigorous experimental methodology with comprehensive ablation studies (Tables 2-4), detailed structural analysis in appendices, and honest discussion of limitations and hyperparameter sensitivity
Well-designed data construction pipeline with multi-stage filtering (consistency validation, topological serialization) that achieves 99.1% quality retention from 10,539 samples
Strong structural validation showing 95% structural faithfulness rate, demonstrating improvements stem from valid logical reasoning rather than spurious label matching
Thorough appendix analysis revealing the 'decoupling' effect where GRPO maintains evidence grounding while reducing inference complexity (correlation 0.85→0.16)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components are established techniques (SFT, GRPO from Shao et al. 2024, teacher-student distillation); the SCM framing is primarily a dependency graph abstraction without actual causal inference, interventions, or counterfactuals

SCM terminology may mislead readers expecting causal inference methods; the clarification in §3.2 is appropriate but comes too late, and the title oversells the contribution relative to what is actually implemented

Hyperparameter sensitivity is substantial with 7-17% performance variation across different settings (Table 4: rcorrect, βs, βl, length ranges), suggesting the method requires careful tuning and may lack robustness across domains

Modest empirical improvements: ~1.4% average gain over best baseline (71.02% vs 69.58%), with some cases showing only 0.86% improvement (HoVer 2-hop: 73.42% vs 72.56%), limiting practical significance

Limited scope and generalization: only evaluated on 2-3 hop reasoning; uncertainty about scaling to longer chains (4+); the core insight about chain length control is somewhat intuitive and not deeply analyzed

Insufficient error analysis: no systematic examination of failure cases, no human evaluation of reasoning quality beyond structural faithfulness metrics, no investigation of when structural guidance helps vs. hurts

Reward function design appears somewhat ad-hoc with questionable component importance: Rs contributes minimally (1.17% performance drop when removed), while Rl dominates (14.7% drop), but length penalties are standard techniques not novel

Teacher model dependency and data quality concerns: reliance on Qwen3-30B-A3B (limited accessibility), unclear how errors propagate despite 0.9% filtering rate, no ablation on teacher quality vs. downstream performance
